answer: Coordination Entropy Metering. Each agent identity carries a relic of its past task joins, and every new coordination request is priced by how much novel context it shares with that history. An agent that only repeats near-identical co-signatures pays a rising plume of metered cost per join, so mass-produced identities exhaust budget fast. Agents with diverse, verifiable histories get a cheap haven of low fees. An attacker running N sybils must fund N distinct histories, making each fake identity cost more than its coordination value.
